subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which tool is used to check that two surfaces meet at a true right angle (90 degrees)?
questions.explain: A try square is used to mark and check right angles between edges and faces.

questions.q: A tenon saw is best described as a saw for cutting which material?
questions.explain: A tenon saw is a small backsaw used for accurate straight cuts in wood.

questions.q: Which tool would be used to cut an internal or external thread onto a metal component?
questions.explain: A tap cuts internal threads and a die cuts external threads on metal.

questions.q: Why is a bench hook used when sawing wood with a tenon saw?
options: It holds the workpiece steady against the bench and protects the surface
It sharpens the saw teeth as you cut
It measures the thickness of the timber
It applies finish to the cut edge
questions.explain: A bench hook supports and steadies the wood, giving safer, more accurate sawing.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a machine such as a pillar drill rather than a hand drill?
options: It produces accurate, perpendicular holes with consistent depth
It removes the need for any marking out
questions.explain: A pillar drill holds the drill vertical, giving accurate and repeatable holes.

questions.q: A student must remove a small amount of waste from a curved internal edge of a piece of MDF. Which tool is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A coping saw has a thin blade that can turn to cut curves and internal shapes.

questions.q: What is a marking gauge used for?
options: Scribing a line parallel to an edge
questions.explain: A marking gauge scribes a line a set distance from and parallel to an edge.

questions.q: Before drilling a hole in metal, a centre punch is used to:
options: Create a small indent to locate the drill bit
Cut the thread for a bolt
questions.explain: A centre punch makes an indent that stops the drill bit wandering when starting.

questions.q: Line bending (strip heating) of acrylic sheet uses a line bender to:
options: Soften a narrow line so the sheet can be folded at an angle
Melt the whole sheet for casting
Harden the edges of the sheet
questions.explain: A line bender heats a narrow strip of thermoplastic so it can be bent along that line.

questions.q: Vacuum forming shapes a thermoplastic sheet by:
options: Heating the sheet and drawing it over a mould using suction
Injecting molten plastic into a metal mould
Rotating a mould filled with powder
Cutting the sheet with a laser
questions.explain: In vacuum forming a softened sheet is pulled onto a mould as air is removed beneath it.

questions.q: Why must a mould for vacuum forming have tapered sides (draft angle) and rounded corners?
options: So the formed part can be released easily and does not thin excessively
So the mould conducts heat faster
So the sheet does not need heating
questions.explain: Draft angles and rounded edges allow the moulding to be removed and reduce webbing and thinning.

questions.q: When shaping wood, what is the difference between a rasp and a file?
options: A rasp has coarse individual teeth for fast removal; a file has finer rows for a smoother finish
A file removes material faster than a rasp
A rasp is only used on metal
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: Rasps cut wood quickly and roughly, while files give a finer, smoother surface.

questions.q: A designer needs to bend a mild steel sheet to a right angle along a straight line. Which process is most suitable?
options: Folding using a folding bar/vice and mallet
questions.explain: Sheet metal is folded along a marked line using folding bars or a vice and a mallet.

questions.q: A batch of identical plastic casings with a hollow shape and uniform wall thickness is required. Which forming process suits mass production best?
questions.explain: Injection moulding forces molten thermoplastic into a mould, ideal for high-volume identical parts.

questions.q: Which of the following is a permanent method of joining metal?
questions.explain: Brazing fuses metals with a filler and forms a permanent joint, unlike bolts or screws.

questions.q: Applying primer, undercoat and topcoat paint to steel mainly serves to:
options: Protect the surface from corrosion and improve appearance
Increase the hardness of the steel
Reduce the weight of the component
questions.explain: Paint systems seal the surface against moisture, preventing rust and enhancing appearance.

questions.q: A mortise and tenon is an example of what type of joint?
questions.explain: The mortise and tenon is a traditional framing joint used in timber construction.

questions.q: Why is quality control important during the making of a product?
options: To check that parts meet the specification and tolerance so the product functions correctly
To remove the need for a specification
questions.explain: Quality control ensures components are within tolerance and fit and work as intended.

questions.q: In manufacturing, what does 'tolerance' mean?
options: The permitted range of variation in a dimension
The total cost of a product
The time taken to assemble a part
questions.explain: Tolerance is the allowable upper and lower limit within which a dimension is acceptable.

questions.q: A wooden toy will be used outdoors and must be protected from moisture while showing the grain. Which finish is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Varnish gives wood a clear, water-resistant protective coating while keeping the grain visible.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Making Principles
